newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU probes Philips /Rabobank know how deal.
newsitem.headline: EU probes Philips /Rabobank know how deal.

text.p: BRUSSELS, April 23 (Reuter) The European Commission said on Wednesday it was investigating whether a 1993 scheme by which Philips Electronics NV sold some of its know-how to Rabobank only to lease it back afterwards involved illegal subsidies.
The operation resulted in tax benefits for the companies which could amount to state aid.

"Additional information is indispensable and the Commission will therefore address a letter to the Dutch authorities requesting full disclosure of the fiscal treatment of the technolease transation of Philips and Rabobank," it said in a statement.
At the end of 1993, Philips sold "certain of its know-how" to the Dutch bank for 2.78 billion guilders of which Rabobank paid immediately 600 million guilders, the Commission said.

The unspecified know-how was at the same time leased back by Philips for a period of 10 years. In return it agreed to pay Rabobank an annual royalty of 140 million guilders. Rabobank is also entitled to half of the proceeds resulting from the granting of licences based on the know-how, the statement added.
Sale and lease-back transactions, which are common for material assets in the aeronautics and property sector, are usually subject to a special tax treatment.

But what makes the transaction between Philips and Rabobank different is that the assets involved are not material. The Commission said it needed to investigate whether the tax rules had been correctly applied in this case.
There is no legal deadline for the Commission to conclude state aid probes. -- Brussels newsroom 322 2876841
